issues.failure_explanation: The energy estimate (test with y, using b(y;y,y)=0) correctly gives ∥∇y∥ ≲ ∥f∥_{H⁻¹}. However the inf-sup pressure estimate includes ∥b(y;y,·)∥_{H⁻¹} ≲ ∥∇y∥² ≲ ∥f∥²_{H⁻¹}, yielding ∥p∥ ≲ ∥f∥_{H⁻¹} + ∥f∥²_{H⁻¹} and not ∥p∥ ≲ ∥f∥_{H⁻¹}. The nonlinear term contributes a quadratic bound that cannot be absorbed into a linear one with a constant independent of f.
issues.overall_effect: The stated linear pressure bound is false for unbounded f. All downstream uses have bounded data (f = u ∈ U_ad), so the weaker quadratic estimate still gives boundedness and every downstream guarantee is preserved.
issues.title: Navier–Stokes pressure estimate is quadratic in forcing, not linear
issues.why_classification: A one-line change to the estimate preserves the existence conclusion and all downstream uses, which only require boundedness for bounded data. No new argument is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypothesis asserts y ∈ L^p where y is the state (always in H² ⊂ L^∞ ⊂ L^p, making the hypothesis vacuous), while the proof uses y_Ω ∈ L^p (the desired state), which is a genuinely additional assumption. The undefined symbol d should be n. As stated, the proof relies on an unestablished premise.

failure_location.quote: Assume that $\mathbf{y}\in \mathbf{L}^{\mathsf{p}}(\Omega)$ for $\mathsf{p} > d$ arbitrarily close to $n$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the hypothesis of Lemma sec_order to y_Ω ∈ L^p for p > n (and replace d by n), and add the same hypothesis y_Ω ∈ L^p to Theorem strictilocalopt.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma sec_order is not proved as stated because the proof requires y_Ω ∈ L^p for p > n, which is not in the hypothesis. Theorem strictilocalopt, which uses the lemma without assuming y_Ω ∈ L^p, has a corresponding proof gap.
issues.title: Second-variation lemma assumes regularity of the wrong quantity
issues.why_classification: Changing the hypothesis variable and adding a standard data-regularity assumption to the dependent theorem are short local fixes. The method, conclusion, and rate all survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The inequality ∥f∥_{L^r} ≲ ∥f∥_{L^1}^{1/r} follows from ∥f∥_{L^r} ≤ ∥f∥_{L^∞}^{(r-1)/r} ∥f∥_{L^1}^{1/r}, which requires f bounded in L^∞. The hypothesis u, û ∈ O(ū̄) ⊂ L²(Ω) does not provide L^∞ bounds; the inequality is false without such bounds (e.g., a spike function of height M on measure M^{−r} has ∥f∥_{L^r} = 1 but ∥f∥_{L^1}^{1/r} → 0). The estimate is valid when u, û ∈ U_ad (bounded in L^∞), as in all downstream applications.

failure_location.quote: Using, in the latter, the estimate $\|\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{u}_{\theta}\|_{\mathbf{L}^{\mathsf{r}}(\Omega)} \lesssim \|\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{u}_{\theta}\|_{\mathbf{L}^{1}(\Omega)}^{\frac{1}{\mathsf{r}}}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis u, û ∈ U_ad (or bounded in L^∞) to Lemma sec_order, restricting its domain from O(ū̄) to U_ad ∩ O(ū̄).
issues.overall_effect: Lemma sec_order is not proved on its stated domain O(ū̄). It is valid on the smaller domain U_ad ∩ O(ū̄), which suffices for every use in the paper (where both controls lie in U_ad).
issues.title: Second-variation lemma proof uses an L^r–L^1 interpolation inequality requiring L^∞ bounds
issues.why_classification: The proof relies on a genuinely false interpolation inequality outside the admissible set; repairing it requires restricting the lemma's domain (a limited weakening). The conclusion and all downstream rates survive, and no new proof architecture is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof asserts without proof that weakly-* cluster points of discrete minimizers ū_h are minimizers of the continuous problem over U_ad ∩ B_ε(ū). Establishing this requires showing (a) uniform convergence J_h → J on U_ad ∩ B_ε(ū) from the state error estimate, (b) lower semicontinuity of J under weakly-* convergence, and (c) passing the discrete variational inequality to the limit. These are non-trivial steps absent from the proof.

issues.title: Convergence theorem omits the non-trivial minimizer convergence argument
issues.why_classification: The missing argument is contained and standard (about half a page of uniform-convergence and lower-semicontinuity steps) but non-trivial. It does not require new proof architecture, and the conclusion and all downstream rates survive once filled in.
